A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hanabi study. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and some plotting inconsistencies in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hanabi benchmarking, prompting ablations, cross-play, finetuning and transfer experiments, plus analyses of human game logs.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and appendix analyses, including Hanabi evaluations, finetuning, transfer benchmarks, and human game-log comparisons.

M1.justification: Watson, Sherlock, and Mycroft retain their inputs, deduction procedures, and memory mechanisms. The SFT and GRPO training procedures and appendix prompts also remain unchanged. Mycroft's method description moves from v1 Section 5 to v2 Section 3.3.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same two- to five-player Hanabi scenarios, self-play and cross-play, HanabiLogs and HanabiRewards training data, and Group Guessing Game, EventQA, IFBench, and AIME 2025 transfer tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and comparator sets are retained. For example, v1 Figure 8 and v2 Figure 7a compare the same Qwen variants with GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 3.7, Grok-3, and o4-mini. SPIN-Bench variants and appendix comparisons also match.

E3.justification: The HLE scoring rules, held-out Qwen evaluation, inference budgets, transfer protocols, and SFT/RL experimental settings are unchanged. The PDFs document no setting revision or rerun that explains the changed graphical quantities.

E4.justification: The prompting ablations, Best-of-K experiments, Mixture-of-Agents comparisons, state-tracking judge evaluation, training-failure analyses, and qualitative examples are retained. v2's separate Failure Analysis subsection reorganizes text already present in v1 Appendix E.3.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed and repetition information, standard-deviation error bars, and Rliable IQM plots with 95% confidence intervals. Changed whisker magnitudes are numerical result changes, without a documented change in statistical reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 and printed mean labels remain unchanged, but some graphical values change. In Figure 3, v2 draws Gemini 2.5 Pro's two-player Sherlock bar at approximately 16.4 rather than v1's 15.4, while retaining the 15.4 label. Other bars and whiskers also differ. The o4-mini SD in v1 Figure 9 versus v2 Figure 7b changes from approximately 2.3 to 2.6. These do not establish experimental performance changes.

T1.justification: The card-state constraints, probability-calculation instructions, and mathematical descriptions are retained. Neither version supplies a theoretical contribution that is added, removed, or revised in the other.

C1.justification: v2's abstract narrows the working-memory claim to top-performing models and explicitly adds that state tracking is unreliable. v1's abstract states more broadly that agents can maintain internal working memory. The main benchmarking, dataset, finetuning, and transfer contributions remain.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement extends discussion to adaptable real-world AI partners, the potential misuse of belief modeling for manipulation, and game environments as safer development settings. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning state tracking, scaffolding, and restricted cross-play coverage are retained.

D1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 newly specifies that Seed 3 was chosen arbitrarily for the prompt ablation. This is a limited disclosure about an existing experiment. Detailed inference settings, training hyperparameters, hardware, seed lists, and prompt templates otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Su et al. (2025), Crossing the Reward Bridge, to support its RLVR terminology, and removes Lewkowycz et al. (2022) and the Luong/Lockhart (2025) reference. Positioning against prior Hanabi agents, LLMArena, and SPIN-Bench remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Mycroft's method and results are integrated into setup and benchmarking, Future Work moves to Appendix A, and an appendix roadmap and Impact Statement are added. The abstract, introduction, and several comparison paragraphs are rewritten, alongside authorship and correspondence edits.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two columns, with extensive resizing and redistribution of displays. Finetuning figures become Figure 7's paired panels; Best-of-K and Mixture-of-Agents figures are similarly merged. The Mycroft schematic moves into the appendix. Several main plots are redrawn, including the Figure 3 inconsistencies described under E6.

improvement.justification: The unified setup, appendix roadmap, and more cautious abstract improve organization and claim calibration. However, v2 introduces multiple bar-height/label contradictions in the central Figure 3 and unexplained whisker changes, reducing the numerical reliability of its empirical presentation. This outweighs the editorial gains modestly; the decline is limited because printed results and appendix evidence are largely preserved.
